# PEBench regression fixtures

These ten source-derived designs are internal schematic/PCB regression fixtures, excluded from the Home catalog and application bundles. Home has nine curated Examples and fixed EMC Flyback Recent; see [Home projects](../../../docs/EXAMPLES.md). Each current structured `.openpe.json` contains an editable schematic, embedded symbols and PCB Layout; adjacent `.kicad_sch` / `.kicad_pcb` files are native KiCad 10 exports generated by the application's serializers. These build-only converters do not provide a general EAGLE or PCB importer in the workbench.

[Manifest](manifest.json) pins repositories, commits, original source paths and SHA-256 hashes. [Source index](upstream-index.json) retains PEBench collection identities and source-provided acceptance/DRC records. Original EAGLE schematics/boards, PEBench-converted KiCad boards, source audits and notices are under [`upstream/`](upstream/). Conversion leaves those bytes unchanged, including `upstream-README.md` and license files. Derived documents retain the individual hardware licenses, independently of OpenPE's software license. [Combined attribution](licenses/NOTICE.txt) and the full [CC BY-SA 3.0](licenses/CC-BY-SA-3.0.txt) / [CC BY-SA 4.0](licenses/CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt) texts are retained locally.

These are educational design references, not qualified zero-DRC benchmark samples. Retained source acceptance/DRC records disclose existing limitations; conversion does not issue new approval. No production validation, ERC/DRC result or PEBench simulation profile is claimed. They are outside the Home/KiCad/TI real-solver sweep.

Fixtures share ordinary [Core](../../../docs/CORE.md) transactions, undo and
Source/revision gates. This does not expand model/import support. The
[fixture overview](../README.md#core-and-capability-checks) separates synthetic
transport coverage from native/solver evidence.

## Reproduce

From the OpenPE repository, with Python 3 and installed Node dependencies:

```sh
python scripts/pebench-schematic.py
npx tsx scripts/build-pebench-examples.ts
```

The Python converter reads the ten pinned local sources and writes `converted/*.kicad_sch` plus conversion audits under `tests/fixtures/pebench/`. `scripts/pebench-schematic.py --collect <PEBench-directory>` is a separate, explicit source-collection step; ordinary regeneration does not read another checkout or use the network. Canonical generation verifies original schematic/board/converted-board hashes and the schematic audit's source hash, then uses deterministic IDs and the current validated project serializer. It writes individual fixture JSON/native exports, [`conversion-audit.json`](conversion-audit.json), the manifest and local notices. It does not update the application catalog. `npm run fixtures:generate` regenerates RC/KiCad/TI fixtures only; PEBench uses these dedicated steps. Do not hand-edit generated snapshots or pinned inputs.

Schematic conversion preserves EAGLE wire geometry, device/gate mappings and physical pad connectivity, with source labels attached to their actual segments. Filled curved artwork polygons are tessellated within 0.005 mm; adjacent artwork rectangles are merged exactly. EAGLE NC pins that are explicitly wired retain those wires through passive KiCad pins. These presentation/electrical-type changes are recorded in `converted/*.audit.json`; they are not an ERC equivalence claim. Source captions and licenses remain embedded.

PCB conversion preserves physical placement, pad shapes/numbers/nets, copper layers, tracks, vias, technical artwork and zone boundaries/settings. The converter omits cached zone fills. OpenPE provides bounded manual copper-zone filling, but it does not implement full KiCad rule parity or DRC. Refill and check native boards in KiCad before manufacturing; viewing/saving does not regenerate fills. Supported geometry remains editable and exports through the validated serializer. See [LAYOUT.md](../../../docs/LAYOUT.md) for preservation, fill and routing boundaries.

## Verification

```sh
npx tsx --test tests/pebench-pcb.test.ts
<KiCad-10-Python> scripts/check-pebench-kicad.py --cli <KiCad-10-CLI>
```

The unit check exercises build-only conversion, native preservation and editable geometry. The native command requires KiCad 10's Python with `pcbnew` and its matching CLI. It exports schematic netlists and compares physical pin groups against the original EAGLE XML, then reopens source/export boards to compare pads/drills/masks/nets/layers, tracks/vias/stacks, board/package artwork/text/captions and zone boundaries/holes/keepouts/thermal/island settings. Equivalent text angles are normalized. Linked Reference/Value captions follow the schematic while retaining source layout; ordinary native text macros remain intact. It also exports schematic/board SVGs.

Detailed native results go to `test-results/pebench-kicad/`; a complete ten-fixture pass records actual version/counts in [verification.json](verification.json). The committed record identifies **KiCad 10.0.1** and structural/connectivity scope. It is not a fresh check of later changes and does not establish ERC/DRC, simulation or manufacturing readiness. No simulation model preparation is required for these PCB regressions. Desktop checks require an explicit user request. Documentation-only edits need static checks rather than conversion or native/desktop execution.
